question: A 55-year-old man presents to the internal medicine clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in his fingers that he first noticed 6 months ago. It has been progressively worsening and has reached the point where it is affecting his normal daily activities, such as brushing his teeth. His past medical history is significant for sinusitis and allergic rhinitis since the age of 18, as well as episodic wheezing and shortness of breath since he was 30. He was diagnosed with asthma when he was 22 years old, and subsequently with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) when he was 40. His current medications include albuterol, loratadine, mometasone, and omeprazole. His blood pressure is 128/86 mm Hg, heart rate is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min. On physical exam, the patient’s skin is mottled and appears to have a diffuse, lace-like, erythematous discoloration of the arms, legs, and trunk. There is also a small papular rash on his right forearm. Bilateral wheezes are heard on auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Allergic rhinitis and sinusitis since age 18 -> Asthma diagnosis at age 22 -> Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) diagnosis at age 40 -> Current medications include albuterol, loratadine, mometasone, and omeprazole -> 70% CHAIN: Numbness and tingling in fingers -> Progressively worsening symptoms affecting daily activities -> Skin mottled with diffuse, lace-like, erythematous discoloration -> Small papular rash on right forearm -> Bilateral wheezes on auscultation -> 80% CHAIN: Skin findings and wheezes on exam -> Consider systemic vasculitis -> 75% CHAIN: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) presents with asthma, sinusitis, skin findings, and peripheral neuropathy -> Most likely diagnosis in this case -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation with numbness and tingling in the fingers, mottled skin with erythematous discoloration, wheezes on auscultation, and a history of asthma, sinusitis, and GERD is highly suggestive of Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (formerly known as Churg-Strauss syndrome). This condition is characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and systemic vasculitis affecting small to medium-sized vessels.
